![{Funding Alert} Healthtech Startup Aignosis Bags Rs 4 Cr to Scale Early Childhood Screening Platform ](https://indian-retailer.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/s3fs-public/2026-10/Untitled%20design%20-%202026-10-01T115001.772.jpg)

Jaipur-based healthtech startup Aignosis has secured Rs 4 crore in a seed funding round led by Antler, Nikhil Kamath, and a group of angel investors, including Varun Dua and IIMA Ventures.

**The newly raised capital will be used to strengthen the company's AI-powered autism and developmental screening platform and expand its reach across India.**

**Founded by Raksheet Jain and Divyansh Mangal, Aignosis previously raised its first funding round in 2024 from investors such as Rajneesh Bhandari and Amit Jain.** The startup has since completed the CDSCO regulatory process and obtained Class B certification. **It was also selected as part of the Google for Startups Accelerator: AI First 2025 cohort.**

**Aignosis has developed an AI-assisted screening solution designed for children between 16 months and nine years of age.** Using a standard laptop and webcam, the platform records a short video session consisting of nine stimulus-based modules. **The system then applies computer vision technology to evaluate behavioural indicators, including gaze patterns, response to name, and reactions to facial expressions.**

**Based on the analysis, the platform generates a risk assessment report that highlights whether a child may require further clinical evaluation.** The company clarifies that the tool is intended for screening purposes and does not provide a medical diagnosis.

**The startup currently follows a Clinic-in-Clinic deployment model and has rolled out its solution across more than 20 government Primary Health Centres in Rajasthan.** It has also entered into a partnership with Mankind Pharma, where the pharmaceutical company's medical representatives support screening camps conducted alongside paediatricians in different parts of the country.

In addition, **Aignosis has begun working with Apollo Shines and is set to introduce its screening services across approximately 125 schools.**

**According to the company, it has conducted over 8,000 screenings to date and is targeting at least 1 lakh screenings by the end of FY27.**

Looking ahead, Aignosis plans to expand its presence into Punjab, NCR, Haryana, Tamil Nadu, Jharkhand, Karnataka, and Maharashtra.

Electric two-wheeler manufacturer Simple Energy has secured Rs 1,750 crore (approximately $182 million) in a Series C funding round, marking the largest capital raise in the company’s history. **The round also ranks among the biggest funding deals secured by an Indian electric two-wheeler original equipment manufacturer (OEM).**

**The investment round was led by the family office of Dr. Arokiaswamy Velumani, founder of Thyrocare Technologies**. Existing stakeholders, including founder and Chief Executive Officer Suhas Rajkumar and co-founder and Chief Financial Officer Ankit Gupta, also participated in the round. **Bengaluru-based high-net-worth individual (HNI) Amit Mishra and the Haran Family Office joined as investors.**

**The fresh funding will be deployed to establish a new manufacturing facility, enhance production capacity, strengthen the company’s distribution and service network, recruit talent, and accelerate research and development efforts for upcoming products.** A portion of the capital will also be allocated toward marketing initiatives and supply chain expansion.

**At present, Simple Energy has a manufacturing capacity of 10,000 units per month and operates a network of more than 80 outlets across over 60 cities in India.** Its product lineup includes the Simple One, Simple Wave, and Simple Ultra electric scooters.

**On the financial front, Simple Energy reported operating revenue in the range of Rs 150–160 crore for FY26, compared to approximately Rs 40 crore in FY25.** The growth represents a nearly fourfold increase in annual revenue. The company currently generates a significant share of its sales from southern India.

**Prior to the Series C round, Simple Energy raised Rs 250 crore through a combination of debt and equity financing in June 2026.** In September 2025, the company secured $10 million through an all-equity bridge round. Earlier fundraising efforts included a $20 million Series A round in July 2024, a bridge funding round exceeding $20 million in February 2023, and $21 million in pre-Series A funding in November 2021.

**Founded in 2019 by Suhas Rajkumar and Shreshth Mishra, the company later added Ankit Gupta as a co-founder.** Simple Energy designs and develops electric two-wheelers along with key components such as batteries, motors, chassis, and software platforms in-house.

Doctor-led longevity and preventive healthcare startup Vytalyou has secured Rs 9 crore in a pre-Series A funding round from investors Chetan Jain of Pharma Dose and Ratan Jain of Venus Industries. **The investment values the company at approximately Rs 33 crore.**

Founded in 2025 by Chirantan Bose and Preetesh Bhandari, Vytalyou focuses on preventive healthcare solutions and longevity-driven medical services. **The company combines diagnostic assessments with personalized health interventions and medically supervised treatment plans.**

Headquartered in Mumbai, Vytalyou offers a range of services including pathology, radiology, cardio-respiratory evaluations, body composition analysis, genetic and cancer screening, gut microbiome assessments, personalized IV therapies, and regenerative healthcare interventions. **The startup also provides non-invasive pain management solutions for chronic musculoskeletal conditions.**

**The company said it has served nearly 1,000 clients since launching its first centre.** Around 50 percent of its customers have come through direct walk-ins, while the remainder have been acquired through referrals and word-of-mouth recommendations.

**Looking ahead, Vytalyou plans to expand its footprint to 10 locations across India over the coming years as demand for preventive healthcare and wellness-focused services continues to grow.**

**Earlier this year, longevity-focused startup Biopeak raised $2.7 million in follow-on funding.** Cent, co-founded by Practo’s Shashank ND, secured approximately $5 million for its AI-driven early detection platform focused on cancer, cardiac, neurological, and metabolic health risks.

**Meanwhile, Elevate Now raised Rs 18 crore in a seed funding round, while Decode Age secured Rs 14.48 crore in a pre-Series A round to advance its work in longevity research, biomarker discovery, multi-omics, and microbiome science.**

Blitz, a startup focused on quick-commerce fulfilment solutions, has raised Rs 28.70 crore in a pre-Series B funding round led by existing investor IvyCap Ventures.

**IvyCap Ventures continues to be the company’s largest external shareholder, holding a 23.47 percent stake.** India Quotient owns 15.31 percent, while AL Trust holds 3.29 percent. ESOPs and MSOPs collectively account for 12.88 percent of the company’s equity.

Primerry, a pediatric healthcare startup focused on children’s wellness products, has secured Rs 7.1 crore (approximately $760,000) in a pre-seed funding round. **The investment will support the company’s efforts to develop child-friendly healthcare solutions and expand its presence across India.**

**Founded by Rushabh Nandu and Dr. Nihar Parekh, the round attracted participation from investors including Ashish Kacholia and Lashit Sanghvi, along with angel investors Mohit Sadaani, Hitesh Dhingra, Ajay Mehra, and Samir Palod, as well as select family offices.**

**The newly raised capital will be used to strengthen the company’s research and development capabilities, expand its leadership team, and increase distribution across key markets.**

**Primerry plans to launch its offerings in phases, beginning with a portfolio of eight SKUs priced between Rs 499 and Rs 1,499.** Products will initially be available through the company’s direct-to-consumer platform, while expansion into quick-commerce channels is planned within the first year of operations.

**Alongside its healthcare products, the startup has introduced PocDoc, a customizable carry case designed to help children organize and carry their wellness essentials.** The company aims to encourage regular healthcare habits by combining functionality with a more engaging user experience.

Primerry plans to establish an offline presence through pharmacies, pediatric clinics, and mother-and-baby specialty stores, with an initial focus on metro cities and Tier-I markets.

> **Nihar Parekh, Co-Founder, Primerry expressed,** *"Over years of pediatric practice, we have seen a clear gap in how everyday health needs, such as growth, immunity, gut health, and coughs and colds are managed. We are building clean formulations with unique delivery formats that rebuild parents' trust. The idea is that wellness must be 100 percent trustworthy, meaning there should be absolutely no doubt in the parent's mind, and that kids should actually enjoy it."*

> **Rushabh, Co-Founder, Primerry stated**, *"Every conversation we had with parents revealed a real want for clean, non-medicated solutions. Our goal is to bring the best global formulations and sourcing standards to parents who are increasingly informed and questioning what they buy for their children. We want to build products that balance what children actually need, ease and fun, with what parents care about most: efficacy and convenience ."*

With fresh funding in place, **Primerry is positioning itself to tap into the growing demand for specialized pediatric healthcare products in India,** as parents increasingly seek wellness solutions designed specifically for children's needs.

![Aman Gupta Invests in FIG Living as Brand Targets Expansion Beyond Lighting](https://indian-retailer.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/s3fs-public/2026-09/Untitled%20design%20-%202026-09-29T124831.815.jpg)

Aman Gupta, entrepreneur, investor, and co-founder of boAt, has invested in FIG Living, a design-focused home and living brand, through his investment firm SailThru Ventures.

**The investment further strengthens Gupta’s long-standing association with Sushant Sharma, founder of FIG Living, who previously worked alongside him at boAt.**

**Established in 2025, FIG Living initially entered the market with a portfolio of lighting products, including table lamps, portable lamps, pendant lights, wall lights, and floor lamps.** Since then, the company has diversified its offerings to include side tables, accent furniture, and tabletop décor products as part of its strategy to evolve into a broader home and lifestyle brand.

**FIG Living currently operates at an annual revenue run rate of approximately Rs 12 crore and has served more than 40,000 customers.** The brand reported growth of around 20 percent quarter-on-quarter and is aiming to achieve an annual revenue run rate of Rs 18 crore following the upcoming festive season.

**The company follows an in-house product development model and has secured more than 36 design patents across its portfolio.** A significant portion of its offerings, nearly 80 percent, is designed using knock-down and do-it-yourself (DIY) formats. **This approach allows customers to assemble products independently while helping reduce logistics costs and improve operational efficiency.**

**With the fresh investment, FIG Living plans to broaden its distribution reach, enhance offline consumer experiences, and create additional customer engagement touchpoints.** The company is also exploring opportunities for international design collaborations and partnerships as part of its next phase of growth.

**Manufacturing operations are carried out in India through an affiliated facility located in Greater Noida.** Going forward, the brand intends to expand its presence beyond lighting and strengthen its position across multiple home and lifestyle categories.

The investment comes at a time when India's home décor and lifestyle segment is witnessing increasing consumer demand for design-driven products, with brands focusing on innovation, local manufacturing, and omnichannel expansion strategies.

Amaani, a consumer-focused beauty and wellness company from the Middle East and parent of beauty brand AÏZA, has secured $5 million in a Series A funding round led by BECO Capital, with participation from Homegrown Ventures and Peak XV’s Surge.

![{Funding Alert} Zelio E-Mobility Plans Rs 167.96 Cr Fundraise to Expand EV Manufacturing](https://indian-retailer.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/s3fs-public/2026-09/Untitled%20design%20-%202026-09-25T170845.285.jpg)

Electric vehicle manufacturer Zelio E-Mobility has announced plans to raise up to Rs 167.96 crore through a preferential issue of equity shares and convertible warrants as it looks to strengthen its manufacturing capabilities and expand its distribution footprint across India.

**The proposal has been approved by the board of the BSE SME-listed company and remains subject to shareholder and regulatory approvals.** The matter will be placed before shareholders at an Extraordinary General Meeting scheduled for October 20.

As part of the fundraising exercise, **Zelio plans to issue up to 9.73 lakh equity shares at Rs 853 per share to four non-promoter investors, aiming to raise approximately Rs 83 crore.**

**Under the proposed allotment, Motilal Oswal Financial Services will receive 4.70 lakh equity shares valued at around Rs 40.09 crore, while Calliope Capital Advisors LLP is set to receive 3.68 lakh shares worth nearly Rs 31.39 crore.** Param Value Investments will be allotted one lakh shares amounting to Rs 8.53 crore, and Hem Growth Opportunities Fund will receive 35,000 shares valued at approximately Rs 2.99 crore.

**In addition, the board has cleared the issuance of up to 9.96 lakh convertible warrants priced at Rs 853 each to promoters Niraj Arya, Deepak Arya, and Kunal Arya.** The warrant issue is expected to generate up to Rs 84.96 crore.

**According to the company, at least 25 percent of the warrant subscription amount will be paid at or before allotment, with the balance payable upon conversion into equity shares**. The warrants can be converted within 18 months from the date of allotment.

**Following the proposed share issuance and complete conversion of the warrants, promoter and promoter group shareholding is expected to reduce from 72.76 percent to 70.87 percent on a fully diluted basis**. Public shareholding is projected to increase from 27.24 percent to 29.13 percent.

**Zelio has appointed SEBI-registered Brickwork Ratings India as the monitoring agency to oversee the utilization of the proceeds raised through the issue.**

**The company stated that the capital infusion will support its nationwide expansion strategy, including the development of its upcoming electric three-wheeler manufacturing facility in Patan, Haryana.**

> “Our next phase is about building the capacity and market reach needed to serve a much larger customer base across India. The proposed fundraise will give us greater room to expand our manufacturing footprint, strengthen our distribution network and accelerate the development of our upcoming three-wheeler facility in Patan. We have built the business with a focus on profitable growth, and the priority now is to take that foundation into more markets while continuing to invest in the capabilities needed for scale,” **said Kunal Arya, Managing Director of Zelio E-Mobility.**

**The EV maker currently operates manufacturing facilities in Haryana, Odisha, and Tamil Nadu.** Earlier this year, the company inaugurated a new production facility in Coimbatore with an annual manufacturing and assembly capacity of 60,000 electric two-wheelers. **With the addition of the new plant, Zelio’s total installed production capacity has reached 2.4 lakh units annually.**

**The company currently works with over 400 dealers across more than 25 states and aims to expand its dealership network to over 550 outlets by the end of FY27.**

Alongside the fundraising proposal, shareholders will also vote on related-party transactions worth up to Rs 50 crore each with Torque Innovation EV Auto Private Limited, AVR Auto Industries Private Limited, Jai Bharat Engineering Tools, Jai Bharat Auto Components, and Rajdhani Machinery Store. **Zelio stated that these transactions, involving the purchase and sale of goods, will be undertaken in the ordinary course of business and on an arm’s-length basis.**

**Headquartered in Hisar, Haryana, Zelio manufactures electric two-wheelers under the Zelio brand and electric three-wheelers under the Tanga brand.**

For FY26, the company reported standalone revenue from operations of Rs 303.54 crore, reflecting a 76.28 percent increase from Rs 172.19 crore in the previous financial year. Standalone profit after tax rose 75.41 percent to Rs 28.03 crore from Rs 15.98 crore a year earlier.

Lab-grown diamond jewellery startup ONYA has secured Rs 12.5 crore in a pre-Series A funding round led by Divisa Family Office, with existing investor Zeropearl VC increasing its commitment by participating again after the company’s earlier Rs 5.5 crore seed funding round.

**The round also builds on support from several angel investors who participated in the startup’s seed stage, including the founders of MyGate, the founder of UrbanVault, and other investors.**

According to the company, the newly raised capital will be used to strengthen its retail presence, drive digital customer acquisition, enhance online personalization capabilities, and expand research and development efforts focused on product innovation, design, and manufacturing.

Founded in 2024 by Gaurav Choudhary and Himani Yadav, ONYA is a lab-grown diamond jewellery brand that combines technology-driven diamond creation with contemporary jewellery design.

**Based in Bengaluru, the company offers IGI-certified lab-grown diamonds set in BIS Hallmarked gold, with a focus on personalized designs and craftsmanship.** The brand states that its products provide consumers with an alternative to natural diamonds at approximately 20 percent of the cost, while also offering a lifetime exchange and buyback program.

ONYA has also developed its proprietary ONYA Setting, a patented ring-setting design, along with its flagship ONYA Signature Collection, which draws inspiration from Neoclassical architecture.

**Since its launch, the company claims to have established a retail network of eight flagship stores across key locations in Bengaluru, Pune’s Amanora Gold Souk Mall, and Hyderabad’s Jubilee Hills.** The brand further stated that it has achieved monthly recurring revenue of Rs 3.5 crore.

Looking ahead, **ONYA plans to enter additional markets through a mix of company-owned outlets and franchise-led expansion.**

The startup operates in India’s growing lab-grown diamond jewellery segment, competing with brands such as Aukera, Limelight, Jewel Box, Fiona, and other players in the category.

**Investor interest in the segment has increased significantly in recent years.** According to industry data cited by the company, nine dedicated lab-grown diamond startups collectively raised $26.4 million in 2025, compared to $4.7 million in 2024.

The sector has witnessed several notable funding rounds, including Aukera’s Rs 90 crore debt raise in July following a $15 million equity round led by Peak XV Partners. Limelight Lab Grown Diamonds also secured Rs 275 crore in a strategic funding round to expand its manufacturing and retail operations, while GIVA, which operates the lab-grown diamond brand Heer, raised Rs 530 crore in a Series C funding round. Other funded companies in the space include Jewelbox, Lucira Jewellery, True Diamond, and Fiona Diamonds.

> **Zeenah Vilcassim, Global Chief Marketing Officer, DailyObjects shared,** *"DailyObjects has already built the foundations of a truly distinctive lifestyle brand: a strong understanding of contemporary consumers and a clear point of view on how design fits into their daily lives. Pankaj and Saurav's ambition to take this India-born brand to the world is something DailyObjects is strongly poised to achieve, with both its local relevance and international appeal. I look forward to joining them on the next stage of this journey, making DailyObjects a brand that is meaningful to consumers' daily lives wherever it goes."*

**The appointment comes at a time when DailyObjects is expanding its global footprint and strengthening its design-focused product portfolio.** The company, which offers technology accessories, carry solutions, workspace essentials, and lifestyle products, recently showcased its offerings at IFA Berlin 2026, marking its first international exhibition and an important step toward building partnerships with global retailers and distributors.

![{Funding Alert} Health and Wellness Startup betterhood Secures Rs 11.5 Cr in Seed Round](https://indian-retailer.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/s3fs-public/2026-09/Untitled%20design%20-%202026-09-24T133311.018.jpg)

Preventive pain care startup betterhood has secured Rs 11.5 crore in a seed funding round led by Sauce, with participation from existing investor Kairon Capital.

**Earlier this year, the Bengaluru-based company had raised Rs 5 crore in the same funding round led by Kairon Capital.** The round also saw participation from Yogesh Kabra, Rishubh Satiya, Rohit Chawla, Sifat Khurana, and Shayamal Vallabhjee.

**The newly raised capital will be utilized to strengthen its product offerings, widen its presence across quick commerce and modern retail channels, and expand its content initiatives and physiotherapist network.**

Established in October 2024 by Vikram Kadam and Neha Zade, **betterhood focuses on preventive pain care solutions designed to address early symptoms of back, neck, and joint discomfort.**

**The brand offers a range of products including posture and ergonomic supports, orthotic soft goods such as back, knee, ankle, and wrist supports, as well as pain relief and recovery solutions.**

**The company said these product categories collectively account for an estimated Rs 20,000 crore market in India and continue to grow at a low- to mid-teen rate.**

As part of its ecosystem approach, betterhood has developed Physio Circle, a nationwide community dedicated to creating awareness around posture, movement, pain prevention, and recovery. The network currently includes more than 7,000 physiotherapists.

**The company has also introduced The Physio Edge, a certification program aimed at helping early-career physiotherapists bridge the gap between academic education and practical clinical experience.**

Since launching operations, **betterhood claims to have served more than 2 lakh customers and created over 1,500 educational content pieces across digital platforms focused on posture, movement, pain prevention, and recovery.**

**The preventive pain management segment has witnessed increased investor interest in recent years.** Nivaan Care raised $7 million to expand its non-surgical chronic pain management clinics, while Litemed’s CURAPOD secured Rs 20 crore in a pre-Series A funding round to scale its photobiomodulation-based wearable pain management technology. **Heatronics also raised Rs 1.8 crore to strengthen its preventive pain management and heat therapy device portfolio.**

**In 2025, Zanskar secured Rs 2.8 crore to broaden its pain care product range and invest in research and development for chronic pain and recovery solutions.** Meanwhile, Stance Health raised $1 million to advance its technology-driven musculoskeletal care platform, which integrates diagnosis, physiotherapy, and recovery programs.

Electric mobility startup Ultraviolette has secured $85 million in a fresh funding round led by Yali Capital and TDK Ventures, with participation from Lip-Bu Tan, Chairman of Walden International, alongside existing investors.

**The Bengaluru-based electric vehicle company plans to deploy the newly raised capital toward scaling production of its flagship F77 and X-47 electric motorcycles, as well as accelerating the rollout of its upcoming products, including the Tesseract scooter and Shockwave enduro motorcycle.**

**As part of its international growth strategy, Ultraviolette is preparing to enter the United States market in 2027 while expanding its presence across Latin America and Southeast Asia.** The company currently markets its electric motorcycles in India and across 20 European countries.

**The latest investment comes shortly after Ultraviolette announced plans for a new manufacturing facility capable of producing up to 500,000 units annually, strengthening its production capabilities to support future demand.**

**The company had previously raised $66 million as part of its ongoing Series E funding round, including $21 million from TDK Ventures and $45 million from Zoho Corporation and Lingotto.** With the addition of the latest funding, Ultraviolette has raised a total of $151 million through disclosed fundraises since August 2025.

Founded in 2016 by Narayan Subramaniam and Niraj Rajmohan, Ultraviolette focuses on the development of electric vehicle platforms and advanced battery technologies. The startup’s investor base includes Lingotto, TDK Ventures, Qualcomm Ventures, Zoho Corporation, TVS Motor Company and Speciale Invest.

**The company has developed battery architectures ranging from 48V to 400V and says its in-house technology stack supports multiple vehicle categories and mobility applications.**

Carry-focused streetwear brand Indian Walker has raised an undisclosed amount in a pre-seed funding round from Palette Wealth Management (PWM), achieving a post-money valuation of Rs 20 crore.

Lifestyle and tech accessories brand DailyObjects is reportedly in the final stages of securing a funding round worth approximately Rs 350 crore, with Xponentia Capital and Anicut Capital’s growth equity fund expected to lead the investment. **The transaction could value the Gurugram-based company at around Rs 1,000 crore.**

**The proposed round is expected to include a mix of primary and secondary share sales.** The fresh capital will likely be used to broaden DailyObjects’ product offerings, strengthen its distribution network, and support efforts to reach a larger customer base.

**The brand has also increased its offline retail presence through exclusive stores, airport outlets, and partnerships with Apple Premium Retail locations.** According to reports, DailyObjects is now available across more than 250 retail locations spanning over 85 cities, including major metropolitan markets and airport retail hubs.

**The company has been investing in both product expansion and offline growth as it works toward scaling revenue and improving profitability.** Earlier this year, founder Pankaj Garg told CNBC-TV18 that DailyObjects expected to close FY26 with net revenue between Rs 215 crore and Rs 220 crore, while targeting revenue of Rs 400 crore in the current financial year. The anticipated growth is being driven by an expanding retail footprint and a broader product portfolio.

The upcoming funding round follows previous investments from firms including Seedfund, Unilazer Ventures, Roots Ventures, 360 One, and Trifecta Capital Advisors. **The company has raised approximately $14.5 million in funding to date.**

**DailyObjects was exploring a fundraise of around Rs 300 crore through a combination of primary and secondary transactions, with Xponentia Capital expected to lead the round.** The latest developments suggest that the size of the transaction has increased to approximately Rs 350 crore, with the inclusion of Anicut Capital’s growth equity fund.

Delhi-based high-protein frozen food brand Protein Pantry has secured Rs 9 crore in a seed funding round led by Sharrp Ventures, with participation from Peercheque, Consumer Collective by Atrium, and Indian Silicon Valley Capital. **The round also saw backing from angel investors including Varun Alagh, Rishubh Satiya, Avnish Anand, Arush Chopra, Saurabh Munjal, Signal Ventures, and others.**

**Protein Pantry has expanded its direct-to-consumer presence across Delhi, Mumbai, Bengaluru, and Jaipur.** The brand is also available on quick commerce platforms including Blinkit, FirstClub, and Flipkart Minutes in Delhi, Mumbai, Bengaluru, and Hyderabad.

![{Funding Alert} Electric Mobility Startup Drivn Secures Rs 45 Cr from Avaana Capital](https://indian-retailer.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/s3fs-public/2026-09/Untitled%20design%20-%202026-09-21T163439.677.jpg)

Electric commercial mobility startup Drivn has secured Rs 45 crore (approximately $4.7 million) in a seed funding round led by Avaana Capital, strengthening its efforts to build an integrated electric mobility platform for commercial transportation in India.

**The funding comes several months after the company announced an $80 million capital commitment from Japanese financial services firm Nomura in February 2026.** While that commitment was made at the group level, the latest investment has been raised by Drivn’s Indian operating entity. The company’s parent holding firm is headquartered in Singapore.

**The board of Drivn’s Indian entity approved the issuance of 33,98,792 compulsorily convertible preference shares (CCPS) at a price of Rs 132.40 per share.** Avaana Capital participated as the sole investor in the funding round, contributing the entire Rs 45 crore.

**The company plans to utilize the newly raised capital to support business expansion, operational requirements, and other general corporate purposes.**

**Founded in 2025 by Manav Bansal and Alpna Jain, Gurugram-based Drivn is focused on developing a full-stack electric mobility ecosystem for large commercial vehicles.** The startup operates in the electric transportation segment by owning and leasing electric intercity buses and heavy-duty trucks, while also providing fleet management and operational services to commercial fleet operators.

**Beyond vehicle deployment, Drivn offers charging infrastructure solutions and battery lifecycle management services, aiming to support businesses transitioning from conventional fleets to electric mobility.**

**Following the latest investment, Drivn Transition PTE. LTD, the Singapore-based parent company, continues to hold a majority stake of 88.75 percent in the Indian business.** Avaana Capital now owns 7.22 percent, while co-founder and Chief Executive Officer Manav Bansal holds 4.03 percent.

**Despite securing funding and attracting strategic backing, the Indian entity remained at a pre-revenue stage during FY26.** Regulatory filings show that the company reported a loss of Rs 1.96 crore during the financial year as it continued to invest in building its operations and platform capabilities.

**The latest funding underscores growing investor interest in the commercial electric vehicle ecosystem, particularly in areas such as fleet electrification, charging infrastructure, and integrated mobility services.**

Ayurvedic wellness brand Ubalance Naturals has introduced a new brand identity, ‘The Forest Within’, as part of its strategy to strengthen its presence in the premium wellness market. **The refreshed identity will be implemented across the company’s portfolio of nine products and 18 SKUs, while supporting its goal of achieving Rs 100 crore in revenue by FY30.**

**The rebranding initiative is inspired by the company’s systems-based approach to wellness, which emphasizes the interconnected nature of the body’s functions rather than treating individual concerns in isolation.** Beginning in September 2026, the new identity will be reflected across product packaging, digital channels, e-commerce platforms, and retail touchpoints.

**Ubalance Naturals develops wellness products that combine Ayurvedic formulations with wild-sourced botanicals.** The brand focuses on processing methods designed to preserve ingredient quality and offers liquid Ayurvedic formulations aimed at convenient consumption and effective nutrient absorption.

> **Gurmeet Kaur, Co-founder, Ubalance Naturals said,** *“Our customers have always trusted us for what’s inside the bottle. Now, the outside reflects the same authenticity and purpose. The Forest Within brings our philosophy of interconnected balance to life through a refined visual identity rooted in nature and true to who we have always been. Building on its established approach to wellness, Ubalance Naturals combines wild-sourced botanicals, careful processing to preserve ingredient integrity, and liquid Ayurvedic formulations designed for ease of consumption and efficient nutrient delivery. As the brand looks to the future, the rebrand will extend across packaging, digital platforms, e-commerce and retail touchpoints from September 2026, creating a cohesive premium experience that reflects the brand’s philosophy and ambitions. We are working towards a bold vision of expanding our reach to 100,000 families by 2028.”*

The company said the refreshed identity is intended to reinforce its positioning within the premium wellness category while creating a unified brand experience across customer touchpoints, including packaging, social media, digital platforms, e-commerce channels, and physical retail environments.

> **Devendra Kumar Oberoi, Co-founder, Ubalance Naturals added,** *“Our purpose has always been rooted in a simple belief: when the body and mind find balance, human potential flourishes. The Forest Within brings this philosophy to life, giving our belief in interconnected wellbeing a new expression inspired by nature. Our identity has evolved, but our purpose remains unchanged.”*

Alongside the brand refresh, Ubalance Naturals has outlined ambitious growth plans. **The company aims to expand its customer base to 100,000 families by 2028 while working towards its long-term revenue target of Rs 100 crore by FY30.**

**The rebranding reflects a broader effort by wellness brands to build stronger consumer connections through purpose-led storytelling, premium design, and consistent brand experiences across online and offline channels.** For Ubalance Naturals, the new identity is expected to support its next phase of growth while reinforcing its focus on holistic wellness rooted in Ayurveda and nature-inspired formulations.

![{Funding Alert} Educational Toys Brand Skillmatics Explores Funding Round After FY26 Growth](https://indian-retailer.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/s3fs-public/2026-09/Untitled%20design%20-%202026-09-21T132341.742.jpg)

Educational toys and learning games company Skillmatics is reportedly exploring a fresh funding round as it seeks to accelerate growth and expand its business operations. **The development comes after the company delivered strong revenue growth while maintaining profitability during FY26.**

**Skillmatics recorded Rs 659 crore in revenue from operations in FY26, reflecting a 34.5 percent increase from Rs 490 crore in FY25.**

**Founded as an educational and entertainment-focused brand, Skillmatics operates a direct-to-consumer (D2C) and omnichannel business catering to children aged one to 12 years.** The company offers a range of educational toys, activity kits, and learning games through its own digital platforms, online marketplaces, and retail partnerships.

**The Mumbai-headquartered company has established a significant international presence, with products available in over 25 countries and distributed through more than 3,000 retail stores worldwide.** North America continues to be its largest market and a key contributor to growth.

**International operations remained the primary revenue driver during FY26.** Approximately 87 percent of the company’s operating income was generated from markets outside India, largely through its US subsidiary, Grasper Global Inc. In addition to operating revenue, **Skillmatics earned Rs 7.52 crore through other income streams, taking its total revenue for the year to nearly Rs 667 crore, compared to Rs 496 crore in FY25.**

**Despite strong top-line growth, the company witnessed a significant increase in expenses.** Total expenditure rose by 36.1 percent year-on-year to Rs 652 crore in FY26, up from Rs 479 crore in the previous fiscal.

**Marketing continued to be one of the company's largest spending categories, accounting for nearly Rs 169 crore, or around 26 percent of overall expenditure.** Manufacturing costs related to toys and games stood at approximately Rs 130 crore, while packaging, logistics, commissions, employee benefits, and other operational expenses also contributed to the higher cost structure.

**As a result of rising costs, profit growth remained relatively moderate compared to revenue expansion.** Skillmatics reported a net profit of Rs 17.57 crore in FY26, up 4.2 percent from Rs 16.86 crore a year earlier.

**The company posted an EBITDA margin of 1.75 percent, while its return on capital employed (ROCE) stood at 5.14 percent during the fiscal year.**

On a unit economics basis, **Skillmatics spent nearly 99 paise to generate every rupee of operating revenue, highlighting the impact of marketing and expansion-related investments on profitability.**

**The company closed FY26 with current assets of around Rs 222 crore, including cash and bank balances of Rs 75.5 crore, providing a solid liquidity position as it prepares for its next phase of growth.**

Backed by investors including Peak XV Partners and Sofina, Skillmatics has raised approximately $28 million across multiple funding rounds.

![LIMIRA Introduces Digital-First Lab-Grown Diamond Jewellery Brand in India](https://indian-retailer.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/s3fs-public/2026-09/Untitled%20design%20-%202026-09-21T112348.141.jpg)

LIMIRA, a newly launched lab-grown diamond jewellery brand, has entered the Indian market with an e-commerce-only business model focused on design, self-expression, and transparency. **The brand aims to offer consumers a digital-first jewellery shopping experience, catering to changing buying habits as more customers research and purchase jewellery online.**

**The launch comes as India's diamond jewellery sector continues to expand.** According to the 2025 De Beers India Diamond Acquisition Study, India now accounts for 12 percent of global diamond jewellery demand, up from 10 percent in 2019, making it the world's second-largest diamond jewellery market.

**At the core of LIMIRA's approach is a gender-neutral design philosophy that encourages consumers to choose jewellery based on personal preferences rather than traditional gender-based classifications.** The brand's positioning is reflected in its tagline, **“Not His, Not Hers, Just Yours.”**

**LIMIRA has introduced four debut collections—****Orbit, Fortuna, Ember, and Eterne****—each centred around a unique narrative.** Orbit celebrates the connection between sisters and close female friendships, while Fortuna reinterprets the horseshoe as a symbol of luck and opportunity. Ember is inspired by meaningful moments and individual expression, and Eterne highlights enduring relationships, memories, and experiences. Through these collections, the brand seeks to position jewellery as a reflection of everyday emotions and personal stories, rather than only major life milestones.

The collection features lab-grown diamond jewellery crafted in 9KT and 14KT gold, available in rose gold, yellow gold, and white gold options. By operating without a physical retail footprint, LIMIRA is placing online discovery and shopping at the centre of its customer journey.

> **Rashmi Gajera, CEO, LIMIRA** said, *“We believe diamonds should not be reserved only for milestones and celebrations. They can be part of an individual’s everyday signature, reflecting who they are, how they feel and how they choose to express themselves. LIMIRA was created to rethink not only the jewellery itself, but the experience of discovering and buying it. Our e-commerce-only model allows us to put design, individuality and transparency at the centre of that experience, while lab-grown diamonds open up new possibilities for how consumers engage with diamond jewellery.”*

**The brand's launch aligns with changing consumer preferences, as jewellery buyers increasingly look for products that resonate with their personal identity, style, and values.** Industry trends indicate that jewellery is becoming less tied to traditional occasions and more integrated into everyday fashion and self-expression.

As India's consumer market continues to evolve, LIMIRA is positioning itself to serve a growing segment of shoppers seeking design-led, accessible, and digitally enabled diamond jewellery experiences.

![{Funding Alert} Healthcare Startup TRUE ARTIS Raises Rs 11.4 Cr for Expansion and Technology Upgrades](https://indian-retailer.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/s3fs-public/2026-09/Untitled%20design%20-%202026-09-16T161356.428.jpg)

Integrated aesthetic surgery platform TRUE ARTIS has secured Rs 11.4 crore in a seed funding round led by Zeropearl VC, as the company looks to expand its presence in the growing aesthetic healthcare segment.

**The funding round also attracted participation from Eleven, a diversified business group founded by Sunil Sachdeva, co-founder of Medanta, along with a group of angel investors.** Several healthcare and startup operators also participated in the round, including Arjun Vaidya, Dhruv Joshi, Ambarish Gupta, and Vivek Lohcheb, Chief Business Officer at PhonePe, as well as former senior executives from Airtel and OYO.

**The fresh capital will be used to establish two new centres in Delhi NCR over the next six to eight months, while also strengthening its surgical infrastructure, recovery facilities, technology capabilities, and patient-care systems.** The company also plans to expand its network of plastic and aesthetic surgeons.

**Founded in 2025 by Ankit Joshi and Sandeep Upadhyay, TRUE ARTIS operates as an integrated platform for aesthetic surgery and cosmetic procedures.** The company combines plastic and aesthetic surgeons, surgical facilities, hospital-grade safety standards, recovery services, and technology-driven patient management under one platform.

**TRUE ARTIS offers a range of services across facial aesthetics, breast procedures, body contouring, hair restoration, and non-surgical aesthetic treatments.** Its proprietary technology platform supports patients throughout their journey, from initial enquiries and consultations to surgery and post-procedure recovery.

**The company stated that it has served more than 10,000 clients and completed over 400 surgeries during the last nine months.** Its facilities are equipped with operating theatres, advanced medical equipment, dedicated recovery units, ICU backup support, and private patient suites.

**To enhance access to specialised care, TRUE ARTIS works with a multidisciplinary network of full-time and visiting plastic surgeons.** This model allows patients to consult multiple specialists through a single platform while receiving treatment under a unified care framework.

**Currently, the company operates two centres in Delhi and Gurugram and collaborates with approximately 20 plastic surgeons across Delhi NCR.**

**The startup also reported a 98 percent client satisfaction rate and stated that its first centre has achieved EBITDA break-even.** According to the company, revenue has been growing at a double-digit month-on-month rate, reflecting increasing demand for specialised aesthetic procedures and cosmetic healthcare services.

![{Funding Alert} Travel and Lifestyle Brand Mokobara Secures Rs 170 Cr Funding](https://indian-retailer.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/s3fs-public/2026-09/Untitled%20design%20-%202026-09-16T122603.303.jpg)

Premium travel and lifestyle brand Mokobara has secured Rs 170 crore (approximately $18 million) in its Series C funding round, led by existing investor Sauce.VC. The round also saw participation from Peak XV Partners, AYRA Ventures, and Niveshaay Investment.

**The fundraise significantly exceeds the** **Rs 91 crore** **the company was reportedly seeking earlier and comes at a time when Mokobara has nearly doubled its annual revenue.**

**Founded in 2019 by** **Sangeet Agrawal** **and** **Navin Parwal****, Mokobara offers a range of premium luggage, bags, and travel accessories.** Over the past six years, the company has expanded its retail presence to more than 52 stores across India while continuing to strengthen its online business. **The brand operates in a growing premium travel accessories market, competing with established luggage companies as well as emerging international brands targeting Indian consumers.**

**Mokobara was last valued at around** **$80 million** **following its Series B funding round in February 2024.** The latest investment marks a notable increase in the company’s valuation.

Sauce.VC contributed Rs 109 crore of the total funding. Around Rs 90.7 crore was raised through the issuance of new preference shares, while the remaining portion included a secondary component. The secondary transaction provides liquidity to employee stock ownership plan (ESOP) holders and members of the founding team.

**The funding follows a strong financial year for Mokobara.** The company’s revenue increased from **Rs 117.4 crore in FY24 to Rs 230.2 crore in FY25**, reflecting substantial growth driven by investments in retail expansion, brand building, and team development.

**The company has continued to invest in strengthening its offline retail footprint, a strategy that has become increasingly important as premium consumer brands seek to build deeper customer engagement beyond online marketplaces.**

**Mokobara’s latest fundraise also highlights growing investor interest in India’s travel and luggage segment.** As more D2C brands establish successful omnichannel operations and expand their physical retail networks, the category continues to attract capital from investors looking to back premium consumer brands with scalable growth potential.

![{Funding Alert} Beauty Startup Firi Raises $3 Mn from 360 ONE Asset and Kunal Shah](https://indian-retailer.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/s3fs-public/2026-09/Untitled%20design%20-%202026-09-16T113822.744.jpg)

Gurugram-based beauty and personal care quick commerce startup Firi has secured $3 million in a funding round led by 360 ONE Asset.

**The investment round also attracted participation from Better Capital, CRED founder Kunal Shah, and several other angel investors.**

**The newly raised funds will be used to broaden the company’s product portfolio by entering categories such as makeup, fragrances, and other beauty segments.** Firi also plans to strengthen its operational footprint by adding more dark stores across Gurugram before expanding into additional markets.

**Founded in 2026 by former Uber India executives Vivek Madani and Karishma Rathaur, Firi operates a curated beauty and personal care marketplace focused on rapid delivery.** The platform leverages artificial intelligence to evaluate product reviews and other data points before selecting products for its catalog.

**According to the company, it has analyzed more than 50 million consumer reviews and shortlisted approximately 3,000 products from the global beauty industry.** The platform currently offers products across skincare, haircare, and body care categories.

**Firi says its quick commerce model enables deliveries in select parts of Gurugram in as little as nine minutes, catering to growing consumer demand for faster access to beauty and personal care products.**

The startup began its pilot operations in January 2026 and officially launched full-scale operations in September 2026. With the latest funding, the company aims to accelerate category expansion and strengthen its presence in the beauty quick commerce segment in India.

{Funding Alert} Fashion Discovery Platform Slayd Raises Rs 1.5 Cr in Pre-Seed Funding Round

![Indian Retailer](https://www.indianretailer.com/themes/custom/menshealth/images/art-logo.webp)

BY - [Indian Retailer Bureau](/author/indian-retailer-bureau)  
 Sub Editor  / 1 MIN READ

[Follow Us ![Indina Retailer](https://www.indianretailer.com/themes/custom/menshealth/images/follow.webp)](https://news.google.com/publications/CAAiEJjETmBVGGR4AF2qcS42jEMqFAgKIhCYxE5gVRhkeABdqnEuNoxD?hl=en-IN&gl=IN&ceid=IN%3Aen)

![{Funding Alert} Fashion Discovery Platform Slayd Raises Rs 1.5 Cr in Pre-Seed Funding Round](https://indian-retailer.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/s3fs-public/2026-09/Untitled%20design%20-%202026-09-16T111524.317.jpg)

Fashion discovery platform Slayd has secured Rs 1.5 crore in a pre-seed funding round led by ajvc, an early-stage investment fund founded by Aviral Bhatnagar.

**Following the investment, the startup has been valued at approximately Rs 16.66 crore post-money.** The fresh capital will be used to strengthen its team and accelerate the growth of its private-label business, Slayd Originals.

**Founded in 2025 by IIT Roorkee alumni Sparsh Jain, Harsh Porwal, and Kumar Prasang, Slayd operates as a fashion discovery platform that brings together products from more than 300 marketplaces and direct-to-consumer (D2C) brands.** The company adds nearly 1 lakh new products every month and leverages a proprietary model that assesses products across more than eight parameters to identify emerging fashion trends.

**The platform has surpassed 200,000 users and achieved more than 40 percent month-one retention.** It also reports that its most active users engage with the platform more than 10 times per month. Currently, Slayd identifies over 2,000 products as emerging bestsellers.

**The platform enables users to explore products across multiple fashion and e-commerce platforms through curated collections and personalized recommendations, helping simplify product discovery in a fragmented online retail landscape.**

In addition to its discovery platform, **the company has expanded into the private-label segment through Slayd Originals, which was launched in beta earlier this year.** The brand is currently generating around 1,000 orders per month, the startup said.

> “India sees more than 1 lakh new apparel designs launched every month across hundreds of fragmented e-commerce platforms. Yet shoppers still have to navigate multiple platforms to discover what's actually trending. Slayd is building the discovery layer for this fragmented market,” **said Sparsh Jain, cofounder, Slayd.**

**The startup noted that insights generated from its product and trend analysis are also being used to identify styles that can be developed under the Slayd Originals label.**

> “Our advantage is that we can identify what shoppers want before building it ourselves. By controlling the design and supply chain, we can bring high-demand styles to customers at better prices, with better quality and a more consistent shopping experience,” **said Harsh Porwal, cofounder, Slayd**.

**With the new funding, Slayd aims to expand its workforce and scale operations for Slayd Originals as it strengthens its position in India’s fashion discovery and D2C retail ecosystem.**

Premium Fashion Brand INTENT Debuts with Activewear and Everyday Essentials

![Indian Retailer](https://www.indianretailer.com/themes/custom/menshealth/images/art-logo.webp)

BY - [Indian Retailer Bureau](/author/indian-retailer-bureau)  
 Sub Editor  / 1 MIN READ

[Follow Us ![Indina Retailer](https://www.indianretailer.com/themes/custom/menshealth/images/follow.webp)](https://news.google.com/publications/CAAiEJjETmBVGGR4AF2qcS42jEMqFAgKIhCYxE5gVRhkeABdqnEuNoxD?hl=en-IN&gl=IN&ceid=IN%3Aen)

![Premium Fashion Brand INTENT Debuts with Activewear and Everyday Essentials](https://indian-retailer.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/s3fs-public/2026-09/Untitled%20design%20-%202026-09-14T143218.995.jpg)

INTENT, a newly launched Indian premium lifestyle apparel brand founded by Arpita Rout, has entered the market with its inaugural collection, introducing a fresh perspective on everyday clothing that focuses on the connection between the body, climate, and modern lifestyles.

**The debut range includes T-shirts, oversized silhouettes, activewear, and everyday essentials designed to transition effortlessly across different aspects of daily life, from work and travel to fitness routines, weekends, and casual wear.**

**At the heart of the brand is its Body Sense Fibre philosophy, which explores how plant-based fibres can enhance comfort and support everyday performance.** Rather than depending on highly synthetic fabrics or overtly technical apparel, INTENT combines natural materials with functional design to create products tailored to contemporary Indian consumers.

**Bamboo-derived fabrics play a key role in the brand’s material strategy.** The fibre has been selected for attributes such as softness, breathability, and a comfortable feel against the skin, aligning with the company’s focus on wearable, performance-oriented apparel.

According to founder Arpita Rout, **the idea behind INTENT emerged from the observation that while people spend most of their lives in everyday clothing, those garments are often not designed around the realities of their bodies, local climate conditions, or daily routines.**

> “I wanted to create something beyond another clothing or sustainable fashion label. INTENT is about natural performance, bringing together thoughtful design, plant-based fibres and the natural abilities of those fibres to create clothing that feels relevant to real life. We live in our everyday clothes, and I believe they should do more than simply look good. They should feel good, move with us, and keep pace with the way we actually live," **shared Arpita, Founder, INTENT**

Created specifically for Indian consumers, **the collection has been developed to address the demands of everyday environments, including heat, humidity, commuting, air-conditioned spaces, and extended hours of wear.**

**The brand’s approach to conscious fashion extends beyond traditional sustainability narratives.** Instead, INTENT places emphasis on material selection, functionality, durability and repeat usage, with the aim of creating premium wardrobe staples designed for long-term use.

**With its market debut, INTENT is positioning itself at the intersection of premium everyday fashion, natural fibres and performance-focused apparel.** The company aims to create clothing that delivers functionality without relying on an overtly technical aesthetic.

> “The future of everyday wear does not need to be louder or more complicated. It needs to be more intelligent, more comfortable, and more intentional,” **added Arpita.**

**The launch collection is now available through INTENT’s official website.**

![{Funding Alert} Furniture Startup Furnishka Raises Rs 26.8 Cr in Extended Pre-Series A Round](https://indian-retailer.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/s3fs-public/2026-09/Untitled%20design%20-%202026-09-14T125902.804.jpg)

Bengaluru-based furniture startup Furnishka is raising Rs 26.8 crore through an extended pre-Series A funding round, with participation from a mix of venture investors, angel backers and startup founders. **Among the notable investors joining the round are PhysicsWallah founders Alakh Pandey and Prateek Maheshwari, along with Udaan co-founder Sujeet Kumar.**

**To facilitate the fundraising, Furnishka has allotted 3,183 preference shares at an issue price of Rs 84,157 apiece.**

**The investment round has attracted capital from Beenext Asia, Bhaarath Sang, Onyx InVen, Amit Jain, Shantanu Jain, Manish Dugar, Mohit Gupta, and Jnabiz Consulting, among others.**

**Bhaarath Sang has emerged as the largest contributor in the round, committing Rs 10.3 crore.** Beenext Asia is investing Rs 3.35 crore, while Onyx InVen and Amit Jain are each contributing Rs 2.37 crore.

**Mohit Gupta and Jnabiz Consulting are investing close to Rs 2 crore each.** Udaan co-founder Sujeet Kumar is participating with an investment of around Rs 1 crore. PhysicsWallah founders Alakh Pandey and Prateek Maheshwari have each committed Rs 1.14 crore. **Shantanu Jain and Manish Dugar are investing approximately Rs 94.3 lakh and Rs 15.1 lakh, respectively.**

**The transaction appears to be part of a broader funding exercise.** While a substantial portion of the committed capital has already been credited to the company’s accounts, the remaining funds are expected to be received shortly.

**With this latest raise, Furnishka’s cumulative funding has reached around Rs 70 crore.** The company had previously secured Rs 27 crore in a pre-Series A round led by IndiaQuotient in October 2024. **That round also saw participation from Sparrow Capital and angel investors, including Sujeet Kumar and Ramakant Sharma.**

**Founded in 2023 by Ganesh Pawar, Furnishka operates in the omnichannel furniture retail space, integrating online commerce with large-format physical stores.** The company offers products across living room, dining room and bedroom categories, with an emphasis on customization, operational efficiency and streamlined supply chain management.

![{Funding Alert} D2C Fashion Startup UniqYou Raises Rs 15.8 Cr to Fuel Growth](https://indian-retailer.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/s3fs-public/2026-09/Untitled%20design%20-%202026-09-14T121931.571.jpg)

Bengaluru-based direct-to-consumer fashion startup UniqYou has secured Rs 15.8 crore in a seed funding round led by Arkam Ventures and Antler. **The investment round also attracted participation from a group of prominent angel investors.**

**UniqYou’s board approved the issuance of 37,487 Compulsorily Convertible Preference Shares (CCPS) at an issue price of Rs 4,215 per share to raise the capital.**

Arkam Ventures emerged as the largest investor in the round, contributing Rs 9.3 crore, while Antler invested Rs 4.96 crore. Angel investor Ankit Garg participated with an investment of Rs 1 crore. **Other investors in the round included Abhishek Goyal, Chaitanya Ramalingegowda, Raveen Sastry and Nandita Sinha.**

**The startup was in discussions to raise approximately Rs 12 crore (around $1.3 million) through a funding round.**

**Following the latest share allotment, Arkam Ventures will hold a 14.93 percent stake in the company, while Antler’s shareholding will stand at 7.96 percent. Abhishek Goyal and Chaitanya Ramalingegowda will own 1.59 percent and 0.24 percent stakes, respectively.**

**UniqYou’s post-money valuation is pegged at around Rs 64 crore, or approximately $6.8 million.** The newly raised capital will primarily be used to support working capital requirements and other general corporate purposes, according to the company’s filings.

**Established in 2026, UniqYou operates in the women’s fashion segment and is focused on building a technology-driven shopping platform.** The startup uses artificial intelligence to track emerging fashion trends and curate relevant products for consumers, aiming to offer a more personalized shopping experience.

**The funding round comes at a time when investor interest in India’s fashion and apparel startup sector remains strong.** Over the past two years, several fashion-focused brands have attracted significant capital to fuel expansion and innovation.

Pee Safe is gearing up for its next stage of growth with plans to broaden its brand portfolio, strengthen its international footprint, expand its quick commerce presence, and explore acquisition opportunities. **The sexual and personal wellness company is also setting its sights on a public listing in FY29-30 while targeting revenue of nearly Rs 250 crore by FY27.**

**Founder Vikas Bagaria said that an IPO continues to be part of the company's long-term roadmap. Pee Safe expects to close FY27 with revenue of around Rs 250 crore, up from Rs 130 crore recorded in the previous financial year.** The company, which posted a low single-digit EBITDA loss last fiscal, is n**ow close to break-even and anticipates turning profitable during the current fiscal year. According to Bagaria, revenue exceeding Rs 200 crore this year would place the business firmly on the profitability track.**

At present, Pee Safe has no immediate plans to raise additional capital after securing $32 million, or nearly Rs 290 crore, in a Series C funding round in January 2026 led by healthcare-focused private equity firm OrbiMed. However, **the company may consider fresh fundraising if it moves forward with acquiring a business or brand.**

The company is also expanding its portfolio through new product launches. **Its recently introduced women-focused nutraceutical brand, Within, has entered the market with three SKUs.** The range includes Inner Bloom, a powdered supplement designed to support gut and intimate health, and Lean Mode, which focuses on appetite management and weight control. 

**Pee Safe projects Within to contribute approximately Rs 5 crore in FY27, growing to Rs 25-30 crore in the following year and reaching nearly Rs 100 crore within the next three years.** Additional products are expected to be introduced by December, leveraging the company’s existing distribution capabilities.

**Pee Safe currently has a retail presence across nearly 55,000 outlets in 100 cities across India and operates in 22 international markets.**

Digital channels remain the primary revenue driver, contributing nearly 70 percent of overall sales. Within this segment, quick commerce accounts for approximately 35-40 percent of revenue.

 Sub Editor  / 1 MIN READ

[Follow Us ![Indina Retailer](https://www.indianretailer.com/themes/custom/menshealth/images/follow.webp)](https://news.google.com/publications/CAAiEJjETmBVGGR4AF2qcS42jEMqFAgKIhCYxE5gVRhkeABdqnEuNoxD?hl=en-IN&gl=IN&ceid=IN%3Aen)

![{Funding Alert} Electric Two-Wheeler Startup Ultraviolette Secures Fresh Rs 373 Cr Investment](https://indian-retailer.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/s3fs-public/2026-09/Untitled%20design%20-%202026-09-11T180531.098.jpg)

Electric two-wheeler manufacturer Ultraviolette Automotive is set to secure an additional Rs 373.04 crore as part of its ongoing Series E funding round, with participation from investors including Yali Capital and TDK Ventures.

**The company will issue 8.15 lakh Series E3 compulsorily convertible preference shares (CCPS) at Rs 2,435 per share, raising approximately Rs 197.5 crore.** In addition, Ultraviolette has allotted 7.24 lakh Series E4 CCPS, generating another Rs 175.5 crore.

**Commenting on the development, the company said,** *“The investments are part of a currently ongoing fundraise; we have nothing further to add at the moment.”*

**Of the total amount being raised, around Rs 249.2 crore is being contributed by Yali Capital’s Yali Deeptech Fund I and existing investor TDK Ventures.** While TDK Ventures first invested in Ultraviolette in August 2025 when it led the company’s $21 million funding round, Yali Capital is joining the startup’s investor base for the first time.

**The funding round has also attracted participation from several angel investors, including Adi Hirji Jehangir, Anshumi Desai, Janak Desai, Mahak Khabia, and Zafar Ahmadullah, among others.**

**The latest investment follows the company’s $45 million Series E fundraise last year, backed by Zoho and Lingotto.** To date, Ultraviolette has raised more than $135 million from investors such as TVS Motor Company, Qualcomm Ventures, Breathe Capital and Mudhal Partners.

**The fresh capital comes at a time when Ultraviolette is accelerating its manufacturing expansion plans through the development of its upcoming BIGGA Factory.**

**The Bengaluru-based electric vehicle maker has outlined plans to invest more than Rs 1,000 crore over the next five years to strengthen its production infrastructure.** Of this, approximately Rs 800 crore is earmarked for the new BIGGA Factory, while an additional Rs 200 crore will be deployed toward expanding its existing manufacturing facility in Bengaluru.

**The company’s co-founders, Narayan Subramaniam and Niraj Rajmohan, previously stated that the new facility will initially have the capacity to manufacture up to 2.5 lakh vehicles annually, with scope to scale production to 5 lakh units in the future.**

**The capacity expansion aligns with Ultraviolette’s strategy to broaden its product portfolio and target larger customer segments within the electric two-wheeler market.** In addition to its premium performance-focused offerings, the company is preparing to introduce new products such as the Shockwave and Tesseract.

**Despite this expansion into broader market segments, the founders emphasized that the company’s long-term vision remains unchanged.**

**Currently, Ultraviolette’s Bengaluru facility has an installed annual production capacity of around 30,000 vehicles.** This is being expanded to between 50,000 and 60,000 units, after which the facility will continue to serve as the company’s engineering, technology and manufacturing hub alongside the BIGGA Factory.

International expansion also remains a key growth priority. **The company expects exports to contribute approximately 25 percent of its revenue over the next five years.**

Highlighting the significance of the new facility, the founders said, *“BIGGA Factory converts that technology foundation into industrial scale,”* describing it as a critical step in Ultraviolette’s ambition to build a global electric mobility business.

**Ultraviolette entered the United Kingdom market with the launch of its F77 motorcycles in November last year and has previously stated that it operates across 12 countries in Europe.**

![{Funding Alert} Triptii Dimri Joins D2C Beauty Startup Peep Beauty as Investor](https://indian-retailer.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/s3fs-public/2026-09/Untitled%20design%20-%202026-09-11T171616.485.jpg)

Actor Triptii Dimri has joined direct-to-consumer eye beauty startup Peep Beauty as an investor and co-creator, strengthening the brand’s efforts to build a dedicated beauty category around coloured contact lenses and eye-focused makeup products.

**Dimri has been actively involved in shaping the brand since its early stages, contributing to creative direction, product discussions, and storytelling initiatives in addition to making a financial investment.**

**Her participation forms part of Peep Beauty’s Rs 12 crore ($1.2 million) pre-seed funding round, which was led by Sadev Ventures.** The round also saw participation from iSeed, ISV and TDV, alongside a group of angel investors.

**Among the angel investors backing the startup are Arjun Vaidya, co-founder of V3 Ventures; Puneet Gupta, founder of Astrotalk; Roman Saini, co-founder of Unacademy; Gaurav Khatri, co-founder of Noise; and Dhruv Bhasin, co-founder of Arata, among others.**

**Founded earlier this year by former Keventers co-founder Aman Arora, Peep Beauty operates in the coloured contact lens and eye makeup categories.** The startup positions itself as India’s first dedicated eye beauty brand, focusing on products designed to enhance self-expression through eye-centric beauty looks.

**The company entered the market with coloured contact lenses as its flagship offering, positioning them as fashion and beauty accessories rather than purely functional products.** Peep Beauty said its lenses have been specifically developed for Indian eye tones and consumer preferences.

**At present, the brand offers coloured contact lenses in five shades, with each pair priced at Rs 399.** It has also expanded into eye cosmetics with the launch of six liquid eyeshadows. The matte variants are priced at Rs 799, while metallic options retail at Rs 849.

Earlier, Aman Arora had indicated that the eyeshadow range was introduced to complement the coloured lenses and help consumers create coordinated eye-focused looks.

**Looking ahead, the startup plans to diversify its portfolio by adding products such as mascara and eyeliner.** The broader objective is to offer a complete eye beauty ecosystem rather than positioning contact lenses as standalone products.

**Peep Beauty also intends to significantly expand its contact lens portfolio over the coming years, increasing the number of available shades to between 15 and 20.** In addition to traditional colours such as brown and grey, the company plans to introduce more experimental shades designed for themed events and occasions, including Halloween.

**As a digital-first business, the startup will continue to focus on its direct-to-consumer platform while expanding distribution through e-commerce marketplaces and quick-commerce channels.** The company also plans to collaborate with creators, makeup artists, dancers, and other cultural influencers to strengthen brand awareness and consumer engagement.

![Actor Vijay Deverakonda Launches Skincare Brand Unhype for Young Indian Consumers](https://indian-retailer.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/s3fs-public/2026-09/Untitled%20design%20-%202026-09-11T155158.718.jpg)

Actor Vijay Deverakonda has ventured into the beauty and personal care segment with the launch of Unhype, a functional skincare brand that he has co-founded and helped develop for the Indian market.

**Targeted at consumers between 18 and 30 years of age, Unhype focuses on unisex skincare products designed for daily use.** The brand’s formulations have been created to address common environmental and lifestyle factors such as heat, humidity, sweat, sun exposure, pollution, and hard water, which are often associated with skin concerns in India.

**Deverakonda played an active role in the brand’s development, contributing to the formulation, testing, and refinement of products before their commercial launch.** The actor reportedly tested multiple versions of the products on his own skin over a nine-month period.

> **Speaking about the venture, Vijay Deverakonda said,** “A year ago, I met a team that had its own R&D and manufacturing facilities, and what stood out to me was that they wanted me to be involved in building the brand, not just be the face of it. That’s what made me want to come on board. We spent months working on the formulations, testing and refining them, and I personally tried every version on my own skin for nine months. We wanted to create high-quality products that are effective, simple to use, and affordable, without all the unnecessary hype around skincare. For me, the idea was to make skincare easy and something people can start incorporating into their routine from a young age.”

**At launch, the brand is introducing two three-step skincare regimens known as the ‘VD Signature Routines’.** Each routine includes a face wash, moisturiser and sunscreen, catering to different skincare needs.

The Acne Safe routine has been formulated for oily and acne-prone skin, while the Brightening routine is designed to address concerns related to tanning and dullness.

**The company stated that all products have undergone independent third-party testing and certification, in addition to real-user evaluations.** The sunscreen formulation incorporates new-generation UV filters and has been specifically developed for Indian skin tones and climatic conditions.

Unhype will debut through online channels, with pre-bookings opening on September 11. Product deliveries are scheduled to commence from September 21, 2026.

![Fashion Quick-Commerce Platform Slikk Launches New Brand Identity and App](https://indian-retailer.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/s3fs-public/2026-09/Untitled%20design%20-%202026-09-11T131313.031.jpg)

Slikk, India’s first quick-commerce fashion platform, has introduced a new brand identity and revamped app experience as it looks to strengthen its position in the online fashion retail space. **The update reflects the company’s efforts to evolve beyond fast delivery and focus on creating a more engaging fashion discovery and shopping journey for consumers.**

T**he rebranding initiative is based on insights gathered from over 2,500 customers.** According to the company, extensive conversations and behavioural analysis helped it better understand how consumers discover, evaluate and purchase fashion products, as well as their expectations from modern fashion platforms.

**These findings played a key role in shaping Slikk’s updated visual identity, app design and broader brand strategy.** The company said the changes are intended to align more closely with evolving consumer preferences and create a more contemporary shopping experience.

**As part of the transformation, Slikk has introduced a refreshed logo, a bold black-led visual identity and a redesigned app interface.** The company believes the new look provides a stronger and more distinctive presence across its digital channels while reinforcing its ambition to become a preferred destination for fashion shopping.

> **Akshay Gulati, Co-founder & CEO, Slikk said,** *“We’ve built Slikk by paying close attention to how people discover, choose, and shop, and our customers have played a pivotal role in shaping where we go next. Speaking to them and analyzing their behavior gave us clear insight into what they want from a fashion platform, an experience that feels relevant, seamless and keeps them engaged. This new identity reflects our growth over the last two years.”*

**To mark the launch, Slikk has rolled out a campaign centered on the brand’s transformation.** The accompanying brand film showcases a series of everyday situations, including a house party, a queue outside a venue, and a Bengaluru traffic jam, where the arrival of a Slikk package triggers a change in mood and atmosphere. **The narrative culminates with the unveiling of the company’s refreshed identity and redesigned app.**

The company said the updated platform aims to offer a more immersive fashion shopping experience by combining product discovery, visual appeal, and convenience within a single ecosystem.

D2C skincare brand Dot & Key has appointed Siddharth Vaya as Senior Vice President & Business Head, a move aimed at strengthening its leadership team as the company accelerates its expansion across skincare categories, omnichannel distribution, and consumer markets.

**The appointment comes at a significant stage in Dot & Key’s growth journey.** The skincare brand recently crossed the Rs 1,300 crore Net Sales Value (NSV) milestone and has recorded a 13-fold growth over the past three years, reflecting its rapid rise in India’s highly competitive beauty and personal care sector.

**With nearly two decades of experience across the FMCG and personal care industries, Vaya brings a diverse leadership background spanning sales, marketing, category management, and business strategy.** Throughout his career, he has worked with direct-to-consumer brands, multinational corporations, and leading Indian consumer goods companies, giving him extensive experience in building and scaling consumer-focused businesses.

**Prior to joining Dot & Key, Vaya served as Chief Business Officer at Beardo, where he was responsible for driving business growth while maintaining a focus on profitability.** During his tenure, he played a key role in scaling operations and strengthening the brand’s position in the grooming and personal care market.

**Before Beardo, Vaya held multiple leadership roles at Marico Limited, one of India’s leading FMCG companies.** He managed the company’s Saffola Oils portfolio as Category Head and also led Marico’s Male Grooming category, contributing to brand growth and category expansion initiatives.

> **Suyash Saraf, Co-Founder & CEO, Dot & Key Skincare said,** “Siddharth brings a strong foundation in FMCG and category leadership, backed by a solid track record of scaling consumer brands. **In his new role, Vaya will lead the business as Dot & Key continues to strengthen its presence in the Indian skincare market.** The company is expected to focus on expanding its category footprint, enhancing omnichannel capabilities, and driving sustainable, profitable growth across its operations.

**Founded in 2018 by Anisha Agarwal Saraf and Suyash Saraf, Dot & Key has grown into one of India’s prominent skincare brands, offering products across categories such as sunscreens, moisturisers, face washes, serums, and lip care.** Headquartered in Kolkata, the brand has built a strong presence through a combination of direct-to-consumer channels, e-commerce platforms, and offline retail partnerships.
